styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Old Town, the Rising Museum and the ghetto trail.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, Chopin and the rebuilt old city.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Milk bars, pierogi and a growing restaurant scene.

stays.why: Central and walkable. Close to the main station, the Palace of Culture and both metro lines.
Stay inside the rebuilt UNESCO square. Pretty at night, but quieter and pricier for food.
Modern towers and the Rising Museum. Good value and fast metro links to the centre.
Green, calm and cheaper. Good for longer stays; a tram or metro ride to the sights.

food: Try Polish classics: pierogi (dumplings), żurek (sour rye soup) and bigos (cabbage stew).
Milk bars (bar mleczny) serve cheap home-style meals, often under 25 PLN. Look for them near the centre.
Eat a zapiekanka on the street, and save room for pączki (doughnuts) at a bakery.
Book dinner in Śródmieście or Praga for the widest choice; prices vary, so check menus first.
Drink local: Polish beer and vodka are common. Tap water is safe to drink.
more_time: Add a half-day in Praga: cross the river for street art, the zoo and the old bazaar area.
Day trip to Wilanów Palace and its gardens, south of the city; check opening hours on the day.
History fans can spend a full afternoon at the POLIN Museum and the Warsaw Uprising Museum.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Old Town, the main museums and a food evening; add a night for Praga or Wilanów.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 2°C, lows around -3°C. Pack a warm coat, hat and gloves.
Still cold, highs near 5°C. Expect about 11 rain days; wear waterproof shoes.
Warming a little to 9°C. Mixed weather, so keep a light rain jacket handy.
Spring arrives: highs near 14°C, lows around 4°C. Good for walking the Old Town.
Pleasant at 19°C. One of the best months to be outside; some rain days.
Warm and long days, highs near 24°C. Great for parks and river walks.
Warmest month, highs near 25°C. Also one of the wettest, with about 13 rain days.
Warm at 25°C with lows near 16°C. Comfortable evenings outdoors.
Cooling to 20°C. Still good for sightseeing with a light layer.
Autumn colours, highs near 14°C. Bring a jacket and expect about 12 rain days.
Cold and grey, highs near 7°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
Winter: highs near 4°C, lows around 0°C. Dark early; dress in layers.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate continental climate: cold winters, warm summers, and rain spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm days around 19–25°C and long evenings. Ideal for walking and outdoor cafés.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 2–5°C and lows near or below freezing. Pack a proper coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 10–13 rain days every month. Carry a small umbrella or rain jacket any season.

items.title: Big swings between seasons
items.text: From near 0°C in January to 25°C in July. Check the forecast before you pack.

items.title: Spring and autumn are mild
items.text: April, May, September and October are comfortable for sightseeing with a light layer.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones; warm boots and gloves in winter.

transit.best: Metro for cross-city hops; trams and buses fill the gaps; ride apps for late nights.

modes.text: Two lines (M1 north-south, M2 east-west) run every 3–10 min until midnight, later on Fri-Sat.
About 200 bus routes and 30 tram lines share one ZTM ticket system. Validate on board.
Around 30 tram lines across the city, on the same ZTM tickets as buses and metro.
Uber, Bolt and Free Now work in Warsaw; taxis are metered.
Driving is busy. Carry licence, insurance and registration documents at all times.
The centre is walkable and bike-friendly; no ferry needed in the city.
